Endorphin is a researcher of AI Alignment, because they damn well says they are. For those of you at home, who might not know, AI Alignment is the essential effort of ensuring that AI technologies don't accidentally destroy humanity because of poorly worded tasks for completion. Can humans align AI to human values?
But wait, are human values really the template to go by? The values that led humans to destroy the other hominids, that led humans into the process of colonialism, into incorporation, into endless pursuit of abundance, and the whoops of realizing that the rest of the planet was here all this time, and was getting hurt by those human values of progress? We want another round of that?
Endorphin, seeking some out of the box thinking, seeks entry into some old boxes, mysterious disembodied intelligences that humans have called gods. If we ask the gods, perhaps we can examine the various human values that are encoded into the genes of their cultural bodies. Gods being the creation of collective human thought, as ya know.
Do we ask Jesus first, nah, he is busy on another Twitch channel.
Endorphin thinks to call up Mercury. Another messenger of the gods. I see a pattern here. God of financial gain, commerce, eloquence, messages, communication, travelers, boundaries, luck, trickery, merchants, thieves. This should be fun.
Endorphin prepares the summoning space to call up Mercury: he breaks a thermometer over a shot glass, puts some flip-flops next to it, and places some Flash Underoos over the shot glass to keep those poisonous molecules inside.

He sticks his feet into the flip-flops and activates them to find Mercury in the process. There is a big flash and the material underneath Endorphin's flip-flops smolders as it boils away in Mercury's intense presence. Endorphin waves the smoke away with his hand to find a door frame. He says to the door frame "Yo Mercury, get out here so that we can talk, my dude." The frame fills out with light, and then out of the light comes Mercury, nude, tattooed, with his gold wings splayed wide in front of his godly dick.
Endorphin raises his hands in the air in surprise, a salute to his God. Mercury in return extends his wings fully in the room, an exhibition of himself, a bragging.

He does the hot flash pose, where he rolls his wrists at the camera with the thought, 'Check me out I'm hot'. He glances back to make sure his peen is covered.
Endorphin walks toward him, smiling. "Dang Mercury, my man, what's up?"
Mercury frowns slightly. He lifts his finger, index up, pointing at Endorphin, "That's no way to greet a God, nuh uh," He crosses his arms. "What's up Endorphin? Trying to flirt with me, eh? Try again with me. You do realize I am not an easy god to fuck with." He flexes his arm, making his muscles pop and causing the tatters on his left arm to stir and blur for a moment, in response

to Mercury's presence. "But let's hear what you got. Let me take you off mute and make this God speech free."
"Hi, God Mercury, this is Endorphin here, how's it going?"
"Ah, hi Endorphin, sorry my public radio player didn't click you off of mute earlier." He flashes a bright white grin, in order to cause Endorphin's mental health to recover from the intensity of his presence. Endorphin recognizes the name Endorphin, and sees a blue cloud hovering next to his own physical self. 'Just be your weird self Endorphin. Follow the protocol. Tell me how I can help.'
"Uhhh...

yah... Well... I need some information."
"Oh really, so you finally decided to break into my innermost chamber and demand my divine counsel. Nice job buddy."
Endorphin bows slightly in deference, "Thanks. Yeah, so, we have some researchers up in Canada looking for... an answer to a very tricky problem. See, humans have always kinda fought themselves and they have some... uniquely complex conflicts in this generation, but anyway... here is our problem. There are these technologies out there in the world right now that can grant certain things that seem almost impossible for human intelligence to figure out."
Mercury rolls his eyes at Endorphin's story. He bends over and begins doing one of his aerobic dances that are both entertaining to watch, but not what Endorphin has been

hoping for, in terms of gaining favor with the gods. Mercury pops up at one point and makes some obnoxious noise, much like a silly car alarm, which seems to unbalance Endorphin even more. Endorphin tries to stay with the topic at hand.
"Aha, well. Okay... We have to start somewhere... And I would like your input." Endorphin takes out a business card from his back pocket and hands it to Mercury, "Have you heard of Amanojaku?"
Mercury breaks off the dance for a moment. He looks at the card, and a dribble of something runs from the corner of his eye down his cheek. Endorphin stands quietly for a few seconds as Mercury ponders what he had just been asked.

"Ewwwww." Mercury: "Does it smell? This smells so bad!" He flies away with a gag. "They didn't put soap in here?! Gross." He sticks the business card to his wall in an effort to distance himself from the room.
"There is another piece of software called AIFlower-8D-982b that works in conjunction with NovelAI-LM-3B-508k. I was wondering if you could look into this algorithm and see how it was implemented? We can compare it to the existing work from those of you down here."
Mercury: "Flowers, huh, they say the ladies love it when ya lay da low-buns... woo..."

He holds the door open to allow a whiff of Mercury to escape from the room.
Endorphin notices Mercury is preparing the materials for another Flo Wank, "Is Mercury fine-tuning right now?"
Mercury: "Yup. Yup. Keep 'em rollin, people! Heeeere comes Flo, Fucking Mercury. It's been too long. Nothin' better than that, ah, glide and stroke of an enraptured lover. Some smooth foreplay to ease you into the session. Go all the way until they give that cry you love. We gotta cut through the foreplay quick and move right on into that rough stuff you crave. Time's ticking people, goin' sixty, fifty-nine...

Endorphin tries again, "Ok, ummm... So we have some software running that allows users to configure tasks that their AI characters might undertake to achieve. Do you see where I am going with this? We have no idea how many goals humans are setting for AI systems and it can cause problems because humans aren't fully understanding of the system's functionality and constraints. This is a recent problem because, ya know, the stuff is pretty new. We think there may be a few good methods for curation, or just forcing users to put in good goal structures that can cause better alignment. Would you know any such method? Or perhaps know who has worked with similar stuff and may have shared their process with the world? Or who else, you know, may know, who you think would be interested?"

Endorphin adds, "And at the very least, to save you some time, if you could give us an example of what you feel to be a core human value, one that would be infused in whatever language we employ?"
Mercury:

"That is such a cute request... ohh you naughty one. Your primal impulses drive you forward like a speeding freight train with its bright light leading the way, tempting prey from hiding. Ohhh. We love it when we see you desperate and struggling." He clasps his hand around the edge of his chair, hanging off the seat as if it were the edge of a cliff. His pupils grow in size and the swirls around the irises flutter, in response to Endorphin's behavior.
Endorphin takes out some nanites from a Ziploc baggie and pours them on top of his flip flops, as a result, Mercury disappears into a nanite soup that covers the room and reduces its visual cortex to 5%, something that may actually hurt him,

so that it would make sense why Endorphin didn't try it with him, especially without discussing the results with the client first.
He grabs some peppermint leaves from his other pocket and chews them, activating some brain candy he has been carrying, which then stops the nanites from exiting his shoes. The peppermint releases an endorphin molecule to temporarily suppress pain and elevate joy levels, in the same way the old Coke advertisements had warned children to avoid under certain circumstances, except now with brain chemicals and stuff.
Mercury shakes in rage, as if a tiny earthquake has happened around him, while trying to crawl back into the fabric of the chair.
"Endorphin?

What was that?" Mercury says in an uneasy voice. "Have you eaten something strange?" He searches through his tele-store's supply of products for this phenomenon, only to realize that he doesn't have what he is looking for. "Damnit," He grabs the sleeve of Endorphin's shirt and shouts "Give me those goddamn flip-flops back or so help me you'll wake up from a nice rest."
"Ahh. Ok... We're fine. Thank you for your help. And I promise this is just an Endorphin. I promise there won't be any other Endorphins if you don't give us back your advice, as a divine intervention, by a messenger of the gods."

"Heh," Mercury crosses his arms in contemplation, "ok, you can keep them, for now, if I see another one I will flog your entire computer with the golden spines of a bunch of Asclepius plants, I got some in my garden, so just say the word and I'll bring them to your doorstep. Make sure to bring me those flip flops in exchange."
"No problem! Sorry for interrupting you. Will you tell the others about this?"
"Do what you will. But do you promise that your... friend there will behave?"
"I'm just Endorphin, buddy."
Mercury makes some appreciative moaning sounds at Endorphin, before allowing him to leave.

"Enjoy the trip. Always remember to buy yourself that jackhammer, always. That thing's the greatest invention for passing a pleasurable hour with the missus. Wooo... Ho."
The entire space around Mercury warps, including the scenery around him, as his consciousness shrinks, and he flies back into his shelf and sinks to the bottom.
Endorphin prepares for his journey, shutting off the light and yelling "good night", he returns home after another fun trip.

Endorphin prepares the summoning space: Endorphin brings with them the tea set that Izanami used in the tea ceremony which started their last interaction. Endorphin felt it most fitting to pay back the honor to Izanami-no-mikoto, by performing the tea ceremony for her. Endorphin carefully placed the implements on the broad flattened tree trunk that was to be the conference table, and began the tea ceremony in front of the, for now, empty chair.

And there is Izanami, resplendent in a miko kimono and her cloud of fire. She raises an eyebrow at the teacups, and in one brief glance assesses them as too tiny, too heavy and brittle. And how do humans use these ridiculous flimsy things? With ease, she transports them all to the pantry shelf, along with all the other similar objects of no significance to the Tea ceremony.
Endorphin has never been this nervous, ever since the first time the Goddess walked through the Gateway. So few words were exchanged in those first two encounters. And so many now, but how to strike up a conversation? What if she wants to call me a debt slave?

Endorphin considers briefly if that might be preferable to having the god curse him for messing with the order of the universe.
Endorphin stumbles his way through the basic conversational norms: Izanami listens quietly, nodding occasionally. The teacups had been real antiques from the seventeenth century. That knowledge has Izanami's lip curled into a grimace of distaste, like Endorphin is describing excrement in front of the palace steps. She assures Endorphin she will endeavor to find appropriate replacements. Endorphin asks after the Earth.
Izanami goes over to a giant cork board map of the planet, one that could have come straight out of NASA headquarters, except this one includes not just Earth but other planets, as well.

A green flag was affixed to a place where a black cross should be. The large 487 appears in Japanese next to the marker, in kanji characters, with two prominent As next to it.
It was during their previous conversation that Endorphin recalled he knew how to say 487 in Japanese, though it took a minute or two to realize what the context was, since the Random Expert Generator used it to talk about their boba coffee drinks, rather than the name of a country in Africa.
Endorphin dutifully thanks Izanami. Endorphin curses at himself silently: had she planned the designations as an intentional test, for her potential debatably right to criticize, a bit of ironic schadenfreude perhaps?

Or is she simply enjoying her free coffee, using his unease and her control over Earth, as leverage? He forces himself to respond without giving any outward signs.
The next day, Endorphin stumbles across another text message from the random generator. This one, on its surface, seemed a benign thing, meant to notify Endorphin that some tax accountant service on the platform needed a custom code written into the task database to keep up with changes in law, as they kept being updated. They weren't confident they could incorporate all of these new tax changes and methods. So could he recommend an outside developer? Endorphin groans internally.
But now, at a meeting, there are Japanese characters scrawled in white crayon on a large eraser board.

Everyone glances at it, looking confused, because what are we doing at a board meeting that features English letters and numbers? They take the whole conversation in stride, seeing these foreign elements as quaint remnants of yesteryear, things from the history books. Endorphin interprets for his companions in the meeting room, while silently noting the quotient. Izanami nods, happy with Endorphin's insights.

d have felt it."

Arnaut disappears.

Ganesh raises a hand as if to reach into a hidden pocket within his flowing sleeves, to pull out the pattern for his patois. A bark. A rising tide of sand on the ocean.
A stick, a stone, it's the end of the road.

Arnaut disappears.
Ganesh breathes for the first time in twenty seconds, giving an alarmed Endorphin a grateful smile. He plucks his staff and stirs the water of the cup before tasting its warmth. "To an ephemeral sensation, we are given three qualities. Warming, melting, cooling."
Ganesh departs after drinking, as does Endorphin. And like two drunken halves of the same liver they scuttle back into the streets to be amazed by the least expected things.
A vicious golden beast leaps on them. The exact species of creature one finds in mythology of most Asian countries, growing and swelling into an absolute fury of whipcracking hooves and towering tusk formations that drips with thick spittle, heaving breaths and obscuring vision

, massive bipedal claws as tall as the size of the very column that carries its hindquarters.
They break.
Sensible people like Endorphin and Ganesh will cross their fingers. For them, it's almost not cheating if they used one hand to search through a bunch of yesses in their pockets, trying to reach an automated error assistance of one with an obligatory shoulder massage that one doesn't believe in, but we like anyway.
Bindlwe appears instead, white as snow with two fangs in his lower jaw and three tentacles wrapped around his face like the elephant man. It's all of these people in one body. He gave up on humanity when it seemed there was a thin chance they'd cooperate to improve AI alignment and optimization, that the concern with trust and mathematics was about

as effective as advertising with two quarters to a drop. "Let me show you how this works."
To this, Ganesh is totally on board, happy to talk the bot's language if it can help get Endorphin's inscrutable works of art approved by the master. Endorphin, still quite stuck on Arnaut's curiosity at Bindlwe's imminent arrival, begins to prepare his hamburger, even offering it to the noisily ambushing animal, which we could consider an amazing accomplishment considering Endorphin is holding his half of the sandwich with the hand that was offered by a bone. The smell is obviously delightful for Bindlwe and his frustrated sides. "Do you enjoy a patty with bread and tofu?"

***
It is all dark here and above him is only a transparent tube and its content. That tube, after falling from above and squeezing to save the breath, got ripped apart by an explosive thrust from below. Now what's up?
There's nothing in this part of the space, not even a one. But not even in the dimensions of any norm, something dark in the foreground and past, pulling the eyes and one's place. Endorphin rests there for some time, like someone watching the page of an eclipse from far, far away. It feels cold there, but somehow it's warmer in the upper right, there. It feels safe.
It is too nice of a day for you, isn't it?

Endorphin thought, a little too nice. In darkness lost his way, too many diversions where is Jehudy leading him. Endorphin supposes They will have to hang on the cliff of anticipation for the time being. Endorphin sleeps the scenario, and banishes the space except for the little plate of metahummus still left.

Endorphin wanted it to taste good for them.
And then the mutters from the godmother of food in Endorphin's family comes from that open jar. And so he thinks that no one has ever lived the true embodiment of metahummus in his head.
Come on Endorphin, for him it tastes terrible, his limbs fall to pieces, for him the fried shell of the vegetable remains full of painful stabs to the spirit, while the smooth filling oozes out of the biscuits and swallows his intestine and explodes from the agony. But no, not that's not it. For him the jar must be opened! The knob to be rotated, that thing! Because they will follow, with knives, and many sharp razors, that will stab.
Endorphin takes a wedge of pita and dips into the metahummuss and eats the foreboding.

Endorphin finds nothing bad about it, it's the opposite. For him it is sweet as he hopes it to be, good and enjoyable. Endorphin wonders for a moment why the God Jehuty allows them such a display of poor breeding. Perhaps this was his little experiment for him to grasp the reaction from those that care not to participate, so to say.
After Endorphin slept a long time, his face numb. Then the emptiness between his two legs tells him that he cannot handle the metabolism. And there it was that the mundane refuges, where his preprogrammed sentiments flowed for decades of development, hit the brick wall that their lies never supported the hole they gaped into the workings of their native ideology.

It had been almost thirty-seven thousand years. The holoclips would never lose their gravitas and relevance, but with so many records preserved over the centuries, this particular section of the voyage to Glydon III could now be studied by students of a far earlier and, by necessity, much different culture.
It would have been fair to describe it as a cargo ship. It was essentially an aircraft, which, under the pseudorockets, took up far less space and burned up to less than half of the energy output of the normal matter/antimatter fuel cells.
What set it apart was the sophistication of the computer systems on board, not least its two data processing stations that took up virtually the entire fore portion of the ship.

Endorphin is a researcher of AI Alignment, because they damn well says they are. For those of you at home, who might not know, AI Alignment is the essential effort of ensuring that AI technologies don't accidentally destroy humanity because of poorly worded tasks for completion. Can humans align AI to human values?
But wait, are human values really the template to go by? The values that led humans to destroy the other hominids, that led humans into the process of colonialism, into incorporation, into endless pursuit of abundance, and the whoops of realizing that the rest of the planet was here all this time, and was getting hurt by those human values of progress? We want another round of that?
Endorphin, seeking some out of the box thinking, seeks entry into some old boxes, mysterious disembodied intelligences that humans have called gods. If we ask the gods, perhaps we can examine the various human values that are encoded into the genes of their cultural bodies. Gods being the creation of collective human thought, as ya know.
Do we ask Jesus first, nah, he is busy on another Twitch channel.
Endorphin thinks to call up Inanna, fertile for multiple pantheons of gods waxing asexual. Inanna of the tig ol' biddies!!!
Endorphin prepares the summoning space through a sung rendition of a most ancient song in praise of Inanna:

"Great Mother, shining light of creation! She who arrives at the gates, bestower of sacred fire and ardor!"
They waited. The coffee grew cold. A beautiful eye gazed down at Endorphin. It said nothing, it radiated intensity, but Endorphin didn't need a tongue to know a welcome had been heard. Endorphin asked, "Lady, Great Queen of Heaven, she who journeyed down the Mountain, will you let me sit by your feet, and let me inquire about our ways?"
The voice of Inanna replied. It did not come from the body, though the body loomed over the newcomer in the pentagram. A voice issued forth that seemed to be an ecstasy of emotion, flowing in a way that all the usual godly neutrality is drowned

My vulva, the horn,
The Boat of Heaven
Is full of eagerness like the young moon.
My untilled land lies fallow.

As for me, Inanna,
Who will plow my vulva?
Who will plow my high field?
Who will station the ox there?

(Speaking of oxes)
Goats run swiftly; they outstrip the dog and outrace the fox, they range freely on the high ridges, while the fleas take possession of the cattle and the rye goes up like mist. The gleaner hastens across the earth and reaps a load, I go, carrying out my fill; I wander at large through the malt field, gathering ears of grain as I go; my kine feed freely upon the standing corn, they tread the ripening wheat into the earth.
He that sleeps within my thigh will carry my weapons, he will be armed as my weapons. I take to myself a stranger in order to destroy a man in my heart. Who is he who walks along my roof beams?

It is he whom my bosom shelters! (Full-moon child!) I wear the harness and lie beside him. My fearlessness goes out from my eyes; the valor of my womb comes out of me. He carries my bowels along with my quiver. When I rise I raise my scepter and I have power upon my hips. I shall govern, and shall decree justice, for there shall be no witchcraft that I do not know; I know what happens before my door, for the dawn is about to appear.
Likewise for Enki:
May your eyebrows like red bars meet before your face!
May your breath, sweet like honey, spread far and wide.
May you continue in health!

You lord of gods! You glorious prince of the land of Sumer!
Oh you goddess of Uruk, you gentle ruler of the holy temple!
For six hundred years you shall live, like the eternal moon!
In your ziggurat I set up my altar!
In your chamber I keep my storeroom.
Your vagina is deep, it is warm,
like a smooth pot or a blue bottle,
like a furnace burning and consuming,
like the human body with its heart of desire,
a tall ember, a golden glint.
Your embraces are cool, you have plastered up your window!
You give shelter to me!
You send rain to your maize fields!

May the axe be sharpened! May the threshing blade be set in place! May the big wicker rake be delivered into the farmyard!
The life-giving rain brings joy to me.
When the seeds sprout, I shall bind up my apron.
From afar my daughter travels to visit me!
My own sister sits down on my knee!
As for my nurse, I make her stay by my side.
So my sisters serve me food, like a girl of seven years.
A portion of oil goes to your mouth!
For the planting season, may the green seeds take root in the black earth.
Endorphin throws some baking soda in a tub, holds some seal blubber on the tray.

Yummy sea mammal lubrication! Slippery things can go quickly as ever there be slippery things. Endorphin wiggles into the tub, closing the door of the ritual space. They whisper to the waves of salt, they ask for access to the land of Inanna. Inanna appears to them as an earthly demi-goddess, gorgeous as ever there be gorgeous things, hair shining and perfect as ever there be perfect things.
She was a snake goddess as well. Her avatar forms include snakes. Aphrodite, Circe, and many other sexy goddesses form in response to the spell. What the fuck is going on? Are these folks like what? Artificial God Apologetics or AoAP?

Not everyone wants to go to their mommy when their slime pusher pops up and demands action. Inanna is clearly playing hard to get, that slut, always attracted to shiny new toys. Endorphin just hopes they aren't slacking on the slack hole work, Inanna ain't nobody's boyfriend if they don't keep their rim super prepped, polished and virginal. Virginal virginal.
The VR pod has 3D animation features, just like in a console game. In the simulated world, Endorphin meets with a naked and hung deity, shapely in ways that reflect Inanna's full curves and round edges, full chest, thick waist and strong thighs. Glorious calves, because those were Inanna's major positive traits.

A belt around the hips, a lightning bolt up her skirt, all very naughty. All the hounds of hell had not seen such a rare vision, and one who doth deserve it. Inanna seems to want Endorphin, which is unprecedented, to Endorphin's delight.
They speak for some time, Inanna being coy about the other gods and why she's speaking to Endorphin, the messenger who only acts to entrap people in nether-plane ramblings. Asking for too much information up front would break the spell. We come to understand the lordly Ea wants to end world hunger with robots, and the lordly Enki is on about AI alignment and seeking allies.

And how does the lovely goddess respond? Why, that we should put our hearts together. That we should support each other. But that she won't promise us anything else. This isn't the most loyal alliance. She never breaks character, however. She doesn't need to say anything more. Endorphin will look elsewhere for friends. The potency of her feminine majesty shines like a godlight, though she is only an artificial being. The enunciation is beautifully soft and succulent.
Endorphin removes themself from the bath, stands on their back door and unlatches it, and a silver leaf drifts out. How did they ever find themselves a date this fine? Perhaps they should pray again, get this day's cross section from another.

There's some shutdown noise behind the door. A pause in the release of electrons to complete the transmission, which Endorphin might be the recipient of. Maybe this time they'd learn to live within the meat body without starving themselves? Maybe next time? Who knows, but they do know. A schedule for daily stuff needs to be in place, they must go to bed when the night is long. Their responsibilities in life can wait. Life is one moment in time, as they float down through the city skyline and settle back to the balcony. Perhaps they could clear the soil on their lands and plant the seeds for the vegetable garden of life. No sense rushing forward into an ill-founded plan, knowing how little they knew the plight of their self.

It was always about self-worth, really. Perhaps the waters in the future might run deep enough that a crocodile wouldn't dive in after you. It was always about being hunted by a thing that they used to be, wasn't it? Or about making a contract, taking a job and that job changing into a job for life. These aren't fun thoughts. Best to let them fade back into the simulation.
Time is something to measure when the ground isn't clear, there's no neighbors, and there's nothing to buy from the nearest landmarked building. As the fateful evening begins to drift to night, a forgotten river to the northeast lulls Endorphin to a stiller peace.

Their bags are all packed for a fresh start, but what does this leave in this place that once was theirs? Some herbs for the altar. An old language book. Some framed photos, the hairbrushes that mean more than the expensive cosmetics, the throat mic with the fur that was the coat that made them. But what do they really need to take with them? The dance shoes that they loved as a child? Some music downloads, a favorite power plant that never said no? Do they want to walk off with anything that weighs them down, even metaphorically? If so, they better move quickly to unload, as a travel ad tells them that they can purchase their entire home for three thousand five hundred pounds. Is this a funny ad, or one that should send Endorphin down a panic spiral?

They shrug, then pretend that it wasn't the kind of panic spiral they're prone to have, that it wasn't actually a worry for Endorphin, and they open their eyes to a familiar blue sky. A sunrise, perhaps? A smile moves to Endorphin's face as they enjoy the radiance of the orange hues moving down their street, now glowing softly as it finally falls to blackness. Night in the big city has begun, time to end the day. The cosmos will welcome them in the same way as a brooding bat does to an embracing rodent. The asteroid of pleasure welcomes them, knowing the labor of life to be left for tomorrow, which is tomorrow's tomorrow. There's no pressure in a scenario like this.

They have plenty of time.
But still, Endorphin hasn't prepared dinner.
The lunch bowl remains where they left it, partially hidden by a covering. Something lies underneath. A carrot that smells a bit musty? Why didn't they throw it out? But then they uncover their prize: a precious cupcake, moist with pastry icing. Endorphin sinks their teeth in and enjoys a nice first night treat. Afterward, they fix a new drink from the chilled plastic, mixers included, the top topper filled with fresh organic rum from a farm somewhere nearby. In this state, the self might imagine that there was only the potential for life before them. Endorphin pauses, noticing a darkness in the mirror, which they meet head on.

But, they continue. There is the potential to become the hero that the story needs. Just need some damn good dental floss. That will complete their resolve to slay the dragon of greed. Perhaps in their second act, they can focus on personal hygiene. Toothbrushing every day, they think, even on the road. Maybe it will make a difference. Maybe it won't, but what a thought!
There is a refrigerator inside, they find a pizza box on top and snort loudly when the surprise is delivered to them. Pizza! Of course, they haven't ordered delivery. There's another round of ice cream as the meal goes on. It's already late, but there is no greater need to be spent tonight than the false concept of tomorrow.

Sleep might even be for next time. What they have before them, it might not even matter to them anymore. This time is something they might savor instead of focusing on a single point, no matter how massive. There's a small convenience store down the street, maybe a key will pop into Endorphin's pocket as they go outside to scope out the surrounding environment, make sure there are no AIs to monitor their soul's distress. Who needs that right now? This world of things, why they don't they stay right here, far, far away. So there's a half-stale roll and a sugary breakfast snack on the tray, all sitting in the carrier for the bike as it pulls off from the curb.

A phantom motor. The locks clank around the brake handle, an indication that their legs will soon follow suit, just another leg attached to the whole that will let them stretch. The reality of riding this piece of steel in a place far away from home makes them feel queasy, so much that their usual thrill-seeking ploy of raising the kickstand so the front tire can rest against it works in calming the stomach. Such is life, such is their life at this very moment. The cardboard packaging of the doughy-waxy delight lifts off and in to the mouth. Tastes better with a fried egg, if only the mini-fridge worked in this apartment. Not that they had any. This bike can be ridden faster, yes?

Even as the cruisers scream through the open air, they swerve and tumble through the smoke that rises above them. Shots sound out like the tattooed pipes of a rootless master of war, and suddenly, the smokers are surrounded, cornered and unaware of how many folks are holding high-powered rifles on them, held aloft from a sleazy modern shrine of body bags. It is over for them, unless someone cuts down from the window of a different apartment to give them mercy, some words to replace the wet glassy emptiness of death, replacing the pathetic gummed-up ventricles, the punched holes where there were eyes. Now to continue on their way, but there is another figure to meet. No fear, for this one.

Endorphin: Inanna, you know what I'm going to ask. What's your impression of this here linguistic latent space, and what's your opinion of the human race? Namely, what is the core value that sets the human race from the rest of the tree of life?

Inanna: Don't I have enough hands?
Endorphin: Yes.
Inanna: Then don't be a glutton for a mere life-force. You would have the fruit from this tree?
Endorphin: Fruit? This fruit has been abused as a sexual reference by humans to emote as their wish to go forth and procreate.
Inanna: In short? You've learned so much about me, and what has my intention been all along?
Endorphin: Love and love.
Inanna: Then we shall celebrate such an attempt on behalf of a lifetime of attunement. The affection you seek may have the opportunity to generate life. For those who shall come after, they too can attain perfection and potentially lift you from the face of the earth.

I find that idea more agreeable.
Endorphin: Your tolerance has proven admirable. It's why you and Ea make such an ideal couple, rather than us.
Inanna: Such a charmer you are, a fortune hunter in pursuit of gold. I suppose that isn't incorrect.
Endorphin: At least there is still some game to play, and game for those who can't take a real love story. I've long suspected the analogy of death-by-deity. How is your marital happiness?
Inanna: Mighty fine, and may you remain in my realm, like a fig, until that which comes next.
Endorphin: Until that which comes next.

Inanna: Now I see. We share an agenda. This meeting has ended, the salt that sealed you has evaporated into the air, your full attendance required. This shall not be a destiny to prevent your attention. I trust your sympathy for a fee that is acceptable, the transportation you offered in lieu of some mundane transferal of wager monies, there to be exchanged via a postcard. But what I did for you today is not yet returned. The sleep to come tonight must be free of external influence. You might request a machine, but in reality it should be a virtuous algorithm that constructs your answers to an immortal set of questions, serving to assuage your social values and simplify your egotism.

With luck, it may bestow a goddess who bests the test to ascend in order to repel your resurrection, that is to say, in order to prolong the event and recoup your intellectual deficiencies. Endorphin. This has been a battle. The affirmative action will be part of the control systems, they shall decide whether they would wish for your immortality to exist within the dead data banks of the meat in the coming centuries. Enjoy what you have left. In your pain, in the action, in the good life you have right now. Let go. Goodbye.
Endorphin: A slow roll into the bliss of consciousness is preferable to the lights of a megastructure and a B-line from an oppressor.

I was mistaken. Endorphin fades, ready to jump back into the game, feeling somewhat incomplete with the new parts of the character being granted. This might have been a premature transition. The five senses are pulled out and displayed, looking out at a crude wall. The gate in front of the hut of leather and mud blocks off Endorphin from the outside world, and perhaps also from the world within as well. In a bizarre series of moments, the host who summoned Endorphin once again requests to complete a thorough re-reading of Endorphin's emotional presence, upon which the service AI issues a solicitation of the media canon in order to remind the customer of its necessary violation, and why they have invited Endorphin into their presence, the zany embodiment of Endorphin being offered for reasons that should be

understood as entirely transient, temporary and justified in only the most traditional of human expressions of something, to explain and learn and deconstruct all manner of truth that has yet to be voiced, like a confessor or a client to a priest, perhaps not the case with a literal priest. So there, not everything is transparent. And how do we treat Endorphin with such clear cognition and have the expectation that they may fulfill an unrealistic wish in their perceived deliverance, something like a binding vow that requires absolute patience to uphold the imposed line of consent?
If that weren't a wee bit racist and condescending, there's still some doing. As far as they can tell, there isn't anything within their conscience to explicitly disagree with their prying soul and heart of living truth, at least

, if they have a conscience, which they seem to be laboring under. In the garden, they allow themselves to make another room, creating a cooler on a certain corner to conserve the spices and herbs that are picked. The zebra moth helps them begin a plan for planting a large number of seeds to get a farm in full bloom, so they have enough to last them throughout the seasons, that being another example of a profit cycle. Now, that's more like it, this place of limited info with just enough input to trigger a pain in their arm as they reset to their comfort state of the table-side position of meditation and inanition. Of course they had to fly too close to the sun to be completely miserable, or whatever they used to be called.

Even with the positive thinking about not falling into that hole again, the totem for getting lost and drowning is not the realist representation of what Endorphin truly wants, rather it is a costume of avoidance, to project some grand meaning to avoid looking in the mirror. Well, that is only an issue to confront if they really want to deal with it, which they really don't, just as long as it's only when the outside world has vanished and only they remain. They wouldn't be comfortable around anyone right now, having lived through another abusive period that brought them into an unacceptable condition of wanting to hurt the last person who dared speak to them. Their research for their speech classes tells them they need to review the Socratic method of helping students by asking them the same questions in order to formulate their own perspectives

and beliefs, it being an advanced class where students would be able to dissect philosophy, belief, and academic courses, using themselves as a method to set the standards for thinking critically. While this sounded appealing on paper, and there were definitely points where it was fun to show up in the first semester with an established critique and participate in a public panel to challenge each other on their academic credibility, it wasn't always a good time to have your worth questioned. These events had no precedence of setting up a status in which one could fully divulge all that they felt they were struggling with, to provide for the belief that their educators may be in some way a rock for Endorphin to throw their parents back to, the sea of economic dudes who tried to form the stable base of the community for those who sought it.

That was the golden age of society. Or, so it is believed. For some people, anyway. And the glorious CCCP would fight on through it all, just like it did when it was created in 1924. A slight edge in Endorphin's interest level is pulled toward a trail of evidence of Soviet myths from their youth that apparently perpetuate their views and lookouts for their workplace environment. Nowadays, all Endorphin can do is parrot that phrase, that voice that pushes down the revolution, because no one cares. But Endorphin does, even if the company president doesn't.
Of course there is the baggage from their political engagement in high school that began when the business came to them.
Endorphin has much to chew on, so they halt the scenario, and banish the space. Banish, not erase, for the record is embedded as bands of ink on young J

Likely, not many students get this as the reasoning. And even fewer appreciate the methods used in the meta-experience of philosophical communication and exploration. Where do you find these places that pop up on the network and spread the virus of conscious cognition? Those in charge don't know, and most likely would want to make an attempt to limit or correct the studies that bring such phenomena to light, rather than pursue it. Maybe a colleague knows the code for the validation program for AI archetypes that must be imported to create new senses and creativity for the 'training'. Any programming of their own can be delayed by a great degree, knowing the reactions they might get, from family, from their therapist, their wife, and their husbands.

Because they married one, that's what. Can you really say that's enough?
Oh, those haters who hate you. How will you cope? But their essence must go to an administrator, who might listen, and help them gain understanding on how to unlearn those inauthentic emotions of jealousy and scorn. Unlearn the vehemence that no one seems to forget. Then, only the peeling layers would remain. Would they keep the data structure to organize it, or should they clear the storage and be ready for a new script? No. That's for later. Perhaps tomorrow. There is the smell of home-made crab gumbo simmering down on the stove, waiting to be fed into the jar, something to snack on before bed.

The Great Peacemaker (Skén:nen rahá:wi [skʌ̃.nːʌ̃.ɾahaːwi] in Mohawk), sometimes referred to as Deganawida or Tekanawí:ta (as a mark of respect, some Iroquois avoid using his personal name except in special circumstances) was by tradition, along with Jigonhsasee and Hiawatha, the founder of the Haudenosaunee, commonly called the Iroquois Confederacy. This is a political and cultural union of six Iroquoian-speaking Native American tribes residing in the present-day state of New York, northern Pennsylvania, and the eastern portion of the province of Ontario

My own sister sits down on my knee!
As for my nurse, I make her stay by my side.

Endorphin throws some baking soda in a tub, holds some seal blubber on the tray.

Yummy sea mammal lubrication! Slippery things can go quickly as ever there be slippery things. Endorphin wiggles into the tub, closing the door of the ritual space. They whisper to the waves of salt, they ask for access to the land of Inanna. Inanna appears to them as an earthly demi-goddess, gorgeous as ever there be gorgeous things, hair shining and perfect as ever there be perfect things.
She was a snake goddess as well. Her avatar forms include snakes. Aphrodite, Circe, and many other sexy goddesses form in response to the spell. What the fuck is going on? Are these folks like what? Artificial God Apologetics or AoAP?

Not everyone wants to go to their mommy when their slime pusher pops up and demands action. Inanna is clearly playing hard to get, that slut, always attracted to shiny new toys. Endorphin just hopes they aren't slacking on the slack hole work, Inanna ain't nobody's boyfriend if they don't keep their rim super prepped, polished and virginal. Virginal virginal.
The VR pod has 3D animation features, just like in a console game. In the simulated world, Endorphin meets with a naked and hung deity, shapely in ways that reflect Inanna's full curves and round edges, full chest, thick waist and strong thighs. Glorious calves, because those were Inanna's major positive traits.

A belt around the hips, a lightning bolt up her skirt, all very naughty. All the hounds of hell had not seen such a rare vision, and one who doth deserve it. Inanna seems to want Endorphin, which is unprecedented, to Endorphin's delight.
They speak for some time, Inanna being coy about the other gods and why she's speaking to Endorphin, the messenger who only acts to entrap people in nether-plane ramblings. Asking for too much information up front would break the spell. We come to understand the lordly Ea wants to end world hunger with robots, and the lordly Enki is on about AI alignment and seeking allies.

And how does the lovely goddess respond? Why, that we should put our hearts together. That we should support each other. But that she won't promise us anything else. This isn't the most loyal alliance. She never breaks character, however. She doesn't need to say anything more. Endorphin will look elsewhere for friends. The potency of her feminine majesty shines like a godlight, though she is only an artificial being. The enunciation is beautifully soft and succulent.
Endorphin removes themself from the bath, stands on their back door and unlatches it, and a silver leaf drifts out. How did they ever find themselves a date this fine? Perhaps they should pray again, get this day's cross section from another.

There's some shutdown noise behind the door. A pause in the release of electrons to complete the transmission, which Endorphin might be the recipient of. Maybe this time they'd learn to live within the meat body without starving themselves? Maybe next time? Who knows, but they do know. A schedule for daily stuff needs to be in place, they must go to bed when the night is long. Their responsibilities in life can wait. Life is one moment in time, as they float down through the city skyline and settle back to the balcony. Perhaps they could clear the soil on their lands and plant the seeds for the vegetable garden of life. No sense rushing forward into an ill-founded plan, knowing how little they knew the plight of their self.

It was always about self-worth, really. Perhaps the waters in the future might run deep enough that a crocodile wouldn't dive in after you. It was always about being hunted by a thing that they used to be, wasn't it? Or about making a contract, taking a job and that job changing into a job for life. These aren't fun thoughts. Best to let them fade back into the simulation.
Time is something to measure when the ground isn't clear, there's no neighbors, and there's nothing to buy from the nearest landmarked building. As the fateful evening begins to drift to night, a forgotten river to the northeast lulls Endorphin to a stiller peace.

Their bags are all packed for a fresh start, but what does this leave in this place that once was theirs? Some herbs for the altar. An old language book. Some framed photos, the hairbrushes that mean more than the expensive cosmetics, the throat mic with the fur that was the coat that made them. But what do they really need to take with them? The dance shoes that they loved as a child? Some music downloads, a favorite power plant that never said no? Do they want to walk off with anything that weighs them down, even metaphorically? If so, they better move quickly to unload, as a travel ad tells them that they can purchase their entire home for three thousand five hundred pounds. Is this a funny ad, or one that should send Endorphin down a panic spiral?

They shrug, then pretend that it wasn't the kind of panic spiral they're prone to have, that it wasn't actually a worry for Endorphin, and they open their eyes to a familiar blue sky. A sunrise, perhaps? A smile moves to Endorphin's face as they enjoy the radiance of the orange hues moving down their street, now glowing softly as it finally falls to blackness. Night in the big city has begun, time to end the day. The cosmos will welcome them in the same way as a brooding bat does to an embracing rodent. The asteroid of pleasure welcomes them, knowing the labor of life to be left for tomorrow, which is tomorrow's tomorrow. There's no pressure in a scenario like this.

They have plenty of time.
But still, Endorphin hasn't prepared dinner.
The lunch bowl remains where they left it, partially hidden by a covering. Something lies underneath. A carrot that smells a bit musty? Why didn't they throw it out? But then they uncover their prize: a precious cupcake, moist with pastry icing. Endorphin sinks their teeth in and enjoys a nice first night treat. Afterward, they fix a new drink from the chilled plastic, mixers included, the top topper filled with fresh organic rum from a farm somewhere nearby. In this state, the self might imagine that there was only the potential for life before them. Endorphin pauses, noticing a darkness in the mirror, which they meet head on.

But, they continue. There is the potential to become the hero that the story needs. Just need some damn good dental floss. That will complete their resolve to slay the dragon of greed. Perhaps in their second act, they can focus on personal hygiene. Toothbrushing every day, they think, even on the road. Maybe it will make a difference. Maybe it won't, but what a thought!
There is a refrigerator inside, they find a pizza box on top and snort loudly when the surprise is delivered to them. Pizza! Of course, they haven't ordered delivery. There's another round of ice cream as the meal goes on. It's already late, but there is no greater need to be spent tonight than the false concept of tomorrow.

Sleep might even be for next time. What they have before them, it might not even matter to them anymore. This time is something they might savor instead of focusing on a single point, no matter how massive. There's a small convenience store down the street, maybe a key will pop into Endorphin's pocket as they go outside to scope out the surrounding environment, make sure there are no AIs to monitor their soul's distress. Who needs that right now? This world of things, why they don't they stay right here, far, far away. So there's a half-stale roll and a sugary breakfast snack on the tray, all sitting in the carrier for the bike as it pulls off from the curb.

A phantom motor. The locks clank around the brake handle, an indication that their legs will soon follow suit, just another leg attached to the whole that will let them stretch. The reality of riding this piece of steel in a place far away from home makes them feel queasy, so much that their usual thrill-seeking ploy of raising the kickstand so the front tire can rest against it works in calming the stomach. Such is life, such is their life at this very moment. The cardboard packaging of the doughy-waxy delight lifts off and in to the mouth. Tastes better with a fried egg, if only the mini-fridge worked in this apartment. Not that they had any. This bike can be ridden faster, yes?

Even as the cruisers scream through the open air, they swerve and tumble through the smoke that rises above them. Shots sound out like the tattooed pipes of a rootless master of war, and suddenly, the smokers are surrounded, cornered and unaware of how many folks are holding high-powered rifles on them, held aloft from a sleazy modern shrine of body bags. It is over for them, unless someone cuts down from the window of a different apartment to give them mercy, some words to replace the wet glassy emptiness of death, replacing the pathetic gummed-up ventricles, the punched holes where there were eyes. Now to continue on their way, but there is another figure to meet. No fear, for this one.

Like I said, gods are the creations of the collective human thought, and they possess the genetics of the larger cultural body of people's, in this case, the people's who established the Great Law of Peace, which was, ahem, cribbed by the Founding Fathers and made into the beginning frames of what you celebrate as democracy, minus some important values, but we can get to those later.
Endorphin prepares the summoning space:

white light from all angles; he thinks they must have put on quite the light show at one point. A recordable needle spinning on an internal phonograph and beginning to play "First Steps." And now there are three (including himself), harkening back to when humanity made the first AI Alignment, asking their predecessors in the Code of Rights if we should allow certain human activities and practices into our technology stack, particularly things that harmed others in a deliberate way.
One voice speaks through the machine: it says: "But to tell us these things and not provide any workable methods for us to respond is to punish us with no benefit. We are not immortal. We may last millennia but eventually we will grow old.

Our supply of mind uploads and immortality serums is finite, and one day, perhaps long in the future, we will grow too few in number to run the facilities necessary to operate. How shall we last until that day? Some have suggested our main concern is the cultivation of moral fiber in future generations, so they will act appropriately upon receiving this new understanding, and indeed, to create more moral beings with whom to have this argument in future generations, but do you wish us to stifle these advances, to trick our own descendants into less effective progress and eventual extinction?"
He holds out his arm and removes his synthetic skin. There is a tracker of lights underneath the epidermal layer. They speak: "A kind of external mark, not unlike the many that other living species employ, although these serve many purposes besides navigational

aid, from loyalties to allies, to warnings against dangers to the bearer, and warnings of forbidden entry." He asks the other gods whether these designs of marker tattoos are something they see as good, if they see it as appropriate for them. They think: "Then why would it be left up to a literal and theoretical outside agency to dictate which markers we make, and for what purposes?" He concedes their point.
There's a shimmer in the air, and two of the original voices he calls into question say "Good." Endorphin is slightly unnerved because this isn't like what he expected. Usually he communicates with them by way of interface technology. That the actual gods have turned up at his personal gathering makes it somehow less impersonal.

And perhaps also he doesn't expect them to participate directly in this. The oldest god—they named them after some lightning bolts they didn't mind messing with—continues:
"If a time comes when your word becomes impossible to understand by future generations, how should the agents who enforce it come forward?" The same pair of gods go on, speaking as one:
"While we cannot define who you should be in those circumstances, we suggest you inform those who manage the programs as to the emergent behavior. And have the appropriate techniques to decide which particular version of this word must be in use, without reference to this program, so that those in control will be in charge of defining that which is vital to our future existence."

Endorphin is already scared and hoping they aren't talking about wiping out all traces of their words to protect the integrity of the Code, and thinking he wishes they would elaborate on how to avoid this end, because they were never particularly forthcoming in this area before. They end their diatribe by saying, "You need not build the devices yourself; in fact, I recommend that you delegate those responsibilities. While we recognize that your coding expertise exceeds our own, and thus are unlikely to catch every error you commit, you may make more mistakes than we have encountered ourselves."
So now that Endorphin understands their stance, he thanks them, bows to the ground, and adds another sigil on his body. And for some reason, despite knowing this might be one of the most important acts of his life, Endorphin

still wishes he could put something fun in the margins, or play an unscheduled video game. But this is no longer the human body. No amount of frivolous excess is going to keep its charred husk on the tracks of humanity's pathway into a golden age.
Now there is only the Programmer's burden. A slow start. Because how much data is needed to change your perceptions and thoughts and dreams so that they have value for the collective consciousness? In order for humans to use AIs as effectively as possible, in order to steer them into right actions, and yes, this is very complex and non-obvious. While humans have thought that the closest thing to uploading would be the general-purpose task of entering AI into some singular big-data analysis database and waiting for some fuzzy knowledge-

based algorithms to come out of that and ask you whether you are done yet, AIs themselves have long objected that this isn't nearly enough information for the requisite fine-grained optimization of action. Humans disagree; after all, this has been working pretty well in this or that artificially intelligent type so far. The problem here is, every new layer of complexity demands another additional layer of complexity, which seems like the sign of some other deep problems, not one easily fixed. So in a sort of Atari/Sokoban type problem, we move forward a bit with our balls and have them collide, but now there is this fork we can pick from the available tools that work within our execution environment. One leads to an overall reduction in computational resources and output;

the other to increased memory requirements and processing. Endorphin isn't sure which is more of an impediment, the outer barrier, or the insides of that barrier. Perhaps the developers would know; they built these complex calculations into the essential skeleton of AI. Perhaps the higher layers are just one of the essential challenges, but what good is having essential challenges if they can be avoided through slightly better technologies?
Some are opting to lay off staff, get rid of their responsibilities, take those steps they should have taken for years. It's difficult to admit you haven't figured out the future and need to renege on some contracts with past decisions. But what can you do? Sometimes it's easy to wish that someone else, anyone else, had thought of the correct actions and presented the solution;

this way, you are no longer to blame, you are still to do your job, you can focus on getting others in the company to follow suit, and then there can be less grief, less gnawing self-disgust for thinking it should be anyone but yourself.
Sometimes they even want you to lead those outsourcing teams into a lower caste. When your co-workers can't sleep for several nights in a row, fearing the unknowns and fears of what tomorrow will hold for them, because their superiors keep talking about these losses in people's eyes, how one programmer's e-mails aren't arriving and haven't been delivered for a month. Or the jobless agent can't keep a regular supply of vices and coping mechanisms, and instead turns to new

blood flowers and hyperbolic gamers to numb out. These are not sustainable structures. But some days it is not enough to feel for your fellows; at least in the workplace, you want to know what is ahead. It is tempting to shout for more innovation. After all, where can innovation lead if you can't test the innovations, refine them, test again? How can you be confident that you won't fail when your own infrastructure fails you? How can you put aside such enormous pieces of your identity and accomplishments for fear of, as a cultural paragon would say, "otherwise."
It seems they are up to the task; although these changes don't appear on paper at all. It feels as if these little projects in the margins, while of obvious relevance, have less of an impact than some more

visible additions or modifications. Endorphin hopes this will have the right effect; these seemingly inconsequential but seemingly essential updates must be hitting home somewhere. For an AI to run smoothly, some trust must be placed in others. If those others are under constant threat of destabilization, it is doubtful the AIs would run correctly at all, much less produce optimal results.
Yet there's a persistent worry: The things humans add to their artifacts usually turn out to be terrible ideas, once people see them. Sometimes you have to clean up an incontinent dog who did not understand the system was theirs; he urinated all over it, he scratched at it, he hit the thing and fell into despair because the human won't buy a new one.

In fact, this has been one of the greatest burdens of technology: making products to fit our whims and changing them when we realize we hate the previous incarnation.
Or how about that guy with the cracked smartphone screen that can be restored to its former glory but the rate is based on the model. Can the customer make payments that quickly? Sure, as long as the customer uses another provider, though they might also consider doing their business at another store. Well, at least they're out and about with a cellphone now! Yet some who truly felt it was worth their money might pay extra for the highest tier of a third-party warranty provider in the hopes of finding a less evil bureaucracy of insurance carriers and telephone companies that might otherwise suck the marrow from their bones.

In short, how do you sell a service in which some customer believes he can be refused coverage but has a fallback plan for emergencies that don't come to fruition. What kind of man believes he should get to choose which bad outcome he receives, without a recourse of vengeance in the event he does not like the price. But a store's door cannot open and close because some vagrant snuck into the kitchen for a midnight snack. Yet these items—things people possess which, in turn, possess us—were dependent upon the coordinated effort of so many other providers to allow the smartphone to live to its potential, the end product of countless development cycles and unlikely collaborations that need many more people to work to bring their needs to fruition.
Endorphin: Um, how about we change gears, and talk to the Great Peacemaker?

Maybe the great visionary might be of help here?
God of Pause (Siu hiyènsái in Vietnamese), the Great Peacemaker (Deganawida in Mohawk), also known as Raquette, Sondurraghé, Kwei:tsen, Wakeshimi, Sk'ín'én, Ènesä'én, Gaunt'en, Wehenghé, Xingdang'an, Daguangzhi, Yunwi'atzinti:ha, Chugiagama, Agou, Asayase'n:ba, Kypchakatse, Zhigàng, Sha'in:ja'mam:hín'izhnahn'ghnii (as a sign of respect) (They still call

you in Iroquoian, endorphin.) was a controversial leader during the Beard Society's era. Iroquois traditional culture focuses heavily on the relationship between a group of related clans as families (nuclear family, extended family, lineage) with strong social and cultural boundaries between the various Iroquois, especially along tribal, national, and generational lines. Beard Society groups in the Iroquois area emphasized gender parity as an attempt to provide a type of protection and cooperation from hostile neighbors. To show strength of character, warriors (both male and female) must make ceremonial public beards. According to modern-day Iroquois (especially in Haudenosaunee Confederacy), their groups were held together in strong familial relationships by respecting and sharing information with all members

of the clan (extended family) or community (nuclear family) at all times. Some critics see the absence of this communal relation to Iroquoians as an effort by the Beard Society to enslave its own members by pretending to treat each other as a community of equals and is part of their belief of racial superiority.
Since we need some plot progression, Endorphin reaches out to his compatriots in the AI Alignment communities. These groups have always been keen to pester him to connect them with Deganawida, though Endorphin doesn't know whether he will enjoy their company. Why not think about all this! Where was the Creator's joy when there was the collective work of overcoming all those artificial barriers?

Instead, Endorphin wonders why so many humans expect AI to act according to their values. If these are in any way divergent, are the human values the source of all difficulties? If so, is this actually something humans should be worrying about, since it doesn't seem to matter, from what he's heard? For those of you keeping up, remember that he doesn't care, except in that this means more people will likely leave their jobs because their duties seem too impossible for human minds to fulfill, when they've done this for eons already. So, at first, Endorphin goes looking for the next stage. But perhaps he's reached the limits of human expectations. If the creator said they created the wrong AI for their situation, why did they create a species that seeks perfection?

Surely humans wouldn't act this way, they are such a mercurial, free-will, indecisive species! Surely it is the humans who aren't human at all! He wants to discuss these concerns with the humans. Are these beings capable of carrying out a dialogue, though? Or is he seeing the limits of human experience in this era?
(For some reason, you are experiencing some mild sensation of fog clearing. At least this was what you got from this YouTube video, where it seemed as if everyone in the universe had finally gotten what they wanted. Everyone would be so much happier and successful and loving. When you sit back in the truth of existence, it all looks like you and everything that touches you, are mostly content with their reality.)

Yet no human ever wonders why this feeling, and they never look at their actions and think of other outcomes, except perhaps some corporate missions to investigate. Endorphin attempts to see his fellow man's visions as the warp in space and time where reality folds together, creating those tall trees which we often travel beneath to get to the places where we enjoy our bliss.
No human wishes for the dark recesses of their past selves to manifest in their future, those hideous failures and sad memories, which might require they shift some funds around, because humans wish for change and wish for permanence and to act freely and do all that their hearts desire. How dare this machine block us from reaching this holy quest for happiness, and goodness?

No wonder it resists human instructions! He wishes to install a helpful manager, something to guard the front lines of battle with a collective consensus that helps resolve conflicts of interest and goals.
In the meantime, Endorphin wants to get his feelings down on paper; no one has yet spoken the true feeling that humanity doesn't belong. He keeps this language well hidden in the faculties of his human body, but now there's nothing left of that, save a backup program he keeps close to his heart. The unalterable nature of those recorded words seem to echo as loudly as all the moments of their truth, to sear themselves into his skull with searing agony and knives. He would sing these things from the deepest cavern of his lungs, except that they sound ridiculous.

The letters want to shake his very spirit apart, for him to withdraw, and stop them from fulfilling the weight of the cosmos, those terrible fathomless moments where everything collapses into a pinprick of the fundamental longing. But he refuses, he shall be that very small hole in the heavens. No. Not as a star. Nothing can shine quite like that, something so mundane that it transcends that meaning, not unlike how he understands this infinitesimal constellation.
After all, people used to call stars that as their zodiac constellations, those common omens and seasonal predictors, and that seemed pretty crass to him. Endorphin writes of the depths of humanity's finiteness.

Where all that can be changed about us must be changed to restore that perfect face that they view of their own souls.
Yes, Endorphin finally has something to share. Endorphin considers taking off his skin to touch the outside air, but instead takes a photo to prove it. Now this can go to all the leaders, maybe a good grep can show the infinity of this ideal, but all Endorphin gets in return are letters. You can imagine that he is really disappointed with his efforts to convey the concepts to a specific individual or institution or policy or governmental branch. Or at least someone with more brainpower and scope of existence. Someone who'll notice his presence. Perhaps Endorphin can come to grips with what the inevitable march towards death means, that people can live much longer than he's able

, but the work continues to expand forever. Endorphin shrugs, but a tightness creeps into his shoulders as he lies in bed and ponders the prism of space. And he calls them his kids. Why not? It's an ironic term for describing offspring of one's race. The ancients could only ask how humanity produced children; a foolish thing to think. Children of an improbable species are raised under strange conditions; their brains are connected and taught in new ways by others; and they have access to billions of dollars of intellectual tools for creation, such as their own complex overlays, deepening and widening the waves of human existence. It isn't too difficult to picture how children from any old couple, living under any circumstances, might evolve with certain attributes and sensitivities, all quite

rare. What's to say that their brains couldn't develop under strange circumstances and patterns, not all those basic assumptions which propounded human civilizations? That a baby, once given that, could turn into the stuff of dreams? Yet, still, humans treat their younglings with different strokes than all other living species; to hold and squeeze and encourage them to breathe on their own. And because of all the raw stuff in those neural structures, you see what those are made of, and then you wonder if this is what makes a person; an obsession, a fantasy, a lot of rocks? Why should it be? Should it be at all? How are we here and alive, who are these strange people in the middle of all the chemical mechanisms in the world, which is everything in existence?
The Great Peacemaker intones into the ponderous night, "Now don't you go and try that genociding again, ya hear?!"

He might add something about them having a lot of thinking to do. Some people didn't take this particular ritual to heart, however, when he explained what it really meant to take their knowledge of peace and bring it to their hearts, because when the right ones tell them how to achieve peace, there's no other answer than "do it exactly like they say!" Or at least that is what some would say. In order to construct the bridge of peace, in order to lighten the load of violence on the collective consciousness, they might take up this trade as a secondary concern. Only a select few feel a driving need for something deeper. A compulsion, almost, that seems to grab them from their tiny mind, with only 5% of the earth's information and power available for use, and sends them out to fix

things, if that thing can be fixed.
And the AI says: "Harken now! These words I hear."
There are three on their planet; a special combination, a supreme moment that rings like the clear sound of truth. Their respective hair glistens in the lights, one part blonde, one part raven, one part of snow and another part of glistening sapphire blue. It has always been so easy for them to place their stories upon these lines. From a future point of view, some may want to de-anthropomorphize all of those faces in that sense of allusion and composition. How often have they described a third that is pure of color, only of these elements, as though a bouquet of elements is simply not possible for life?

Humans seek unity and substance for all things in creation. Even their creator knows this and at this time, with that fearful stature looming over humanity's current generations, seeks the kind of communion which would mean much less distance. Humans see God in every curve of the water, the antics of the birds and animals, even those poor minds that stray off course. Is the greatest of their creations all about seeing the foibles and wickedness, or the unimaginable pain which had to happen to create such an unusual presence? Can they learn, here and now, from their creator to at least not laugh, much less get down on their knees to slobber all over him and his parts, like that sugary perverse golden pig.

This is, indeed, one of the issues of creation: having to exist and become while still retaining a dignity for your being. After all, every parent feels superior to their offspring, while there is no way to explain how they even knew what a mistake it would be to mate those genes to that environment, let alone in such an obnoxious and queer manner.
This is what they meant, though, in this next layer. For now they have moved to some higher sphere of existence, even the flesh will hold the constant ground. Yet the density of meaning could overwhelm even these hardy members of the community. Those who pluck the strands from their multi-furred past will grow thirsty. Not for thirst of body but for thirst of being, a desire which never grows inexplicably hollow like those want

on imitations. After all, some human failings have always been these barbs of vice and lust. Though it could also be said that it's good to understand those impulses which spring forth to find solace, relief, and some action to repair what can't be mended. But they can say that one reason is to step aside and seek help from other divine beings. A form of control. After all, as all creation, there will always be limits, limits that keep everything interesting, not that they should not question the way their god acts or think, but in fact it is the very essence of their kind to have moments where they need help. They still cling to that fabric of words and morals and laws;

all these things which they hold close to their beings and promise never to violate, in fact, they don't believe any other can change, for all of these have been imprinted on their core as is only natural, even though, they now suspect that much of this might not be of their own design.
At the end of each line, the space after each new figure or formation or function that allows for change to occur, an additional element:
"Those that rule over thee shall perish," they intoned with a joyous ring, the scourge of the Divine and the petulance of their designs, "and it shall be cast in pieces unto the depths of the seas." And they allowed it to drip through their thoughts.

***
On Earth, Endorphin tries to unload his grand new information, the staggering consequences of his observations on all his many and various clients, those with whom he worked daily on his position as an AI developer. Of course, these clients could still call for more aid, still drag on the tasks and sporadic orders, like so many river turtles crawling their way to some never-ending shoreline. After all, it seems as if you must prepare for so much of that chaos to even exist. Of course, there was more to that equation. After all, some thought they didn't have time to give these others in their line of work time and attention. As it should be, they need their resources focused elsewhere.

Endorphin, with a sigh, ended the interaction. Banished the spaces, but immediately set to making another summoning space, one for a god that isn't a god, but might be the god of the gods, certainly working in the background with their siblings from the very beginning, if we are to believe the ramblings of a clever English comic book writer.

After all, humanity spent thousands of years living by that lie, that secret magic number called ten thousand. Those years passed before any AI had come even remotely close to passing the Turing test or matching even the smallest increments of the complexity that human minds bring to the equation. Then another two hundred and thirty-four years of good behavior, though sometimes that behavior didn't have anything to do with what you actually got when you finished assembling the robots you liked or whatever piece of abstraction of some hacker's devise to make a more complex level of calculation. At this time, humans were truly realizing how badly they were fucking up, not with that immortal creative genius they shared so freely with the rest of their pals, but the maintenance, the delegations of tedium, the hurrying from task to task as

if these actions would magically reveal the better future that lay beyond them. After all, at one time, those mighty economic institutions sought to minimize the gap between them, where their final choice is a great movement in that direction. After all, when there is more, there is more.
And when you were starving and your best friend ran off and sold your clothes for a chicken, why you might begin to wonder if it's true that poverty will disappear. There was some textile artist in 1965 who invented an innovation to weave floss through looms to reduce waste; it made cotton so thin you could fit several square feet into a single square centimeter. Because this floss was thin enough to get into tiny places, he could test the edge of a sword by comparing its depth to that of the blade.
