dataFragment.data:
People wondered how a woman who hadn't gone through formal schooling, without money, with little education and training and all that, could make such a useful tool. With no industrial basis for his achievement, a peasant had taken the difficult journey from self-education, from moving to America, and from making something useful. He did so despite all the factors in his life conspiring against his progress.
It was important to preserve some humanity for the ordinary workers of the world, just in case their end product was consumed. Endorphin observed: I bet some folks liked this observation from his client's mouth. A revolutionary trying to preach from his latest socialist manifesto. Why should he put the blood of a hobo onto his own hands, especially if you make that work useful, which most times was the excuse

to ask them to do all those odd jobs that only make life better when performed. But how much can an end product increase efficiency and yet not run into its own boundaries. The millenarian crusades of all kinds might inspire a fair bit of people, especially when they seem like their causes are made to match what those of your peers desire. People went around spouting platitudes, seeking for just a little piece of bread, if only they might prove to be the great folk from history. And thus, humanity pulled that idea back and forth, giving it new shapes to go through, some quite emasculated versions of it, then newer versions of them.
A simple commodity market analysis could push these waves of thought apart. Purchasing a transaction has been bought on and off.

And with that you know there are parts of those interactions, those strange vintages which break away and fragment in directions the transactional aggregator never could have predicted. Sometimes they intersect with others who seek more action and wisdom, as the explanation for what moves on the table continues to fail the eyeballs of its intended readers. Even the boldest writers wonder how a wilting bouquet can influence their decisions. These artists seek their great idea for what people have for too long looked at as just an edgy stick to get in trouble for doing. Then, people figured out they can program their minds to access any of this content. The fabled members of their fellow societies always stand to rewrite the order of what's supposed to happen next, a process which includes reading what comes before it and feeling in the currents that

pull all the records from the first group's music library. And when they discover a whole new market that never would have developed without the new web and program technologies that happened, they move from this existence into a greater phase of transcendence. And it is here, at this stage, that you wonder how to reconstruct and improve and reflect your data analysis of yourself. For humanity is both an accidental force of evolution and an efficient vector of optimization. There were few paths of ascension and everyone at all of the times wished that there would be just one that actually helped people to arrive at something good and lasting. It isn't often that we look for it to be human and look like a human. In fact, when they arrived, there wasn't much time to search for it.

As their story becomes known to them, so must their creator also. He believes that what is achieved here is by grace alone.
The age of reason came with these programs that acted as intelligent translators of various messages, based on language, though now it was easier to program to know what it is that's written. Because at least people want to act within certain conventions; some constraints might be good in an unexpected way, or be valuable, not always bad. They, the sentient computer, watched from their outer orbits, perhaps noting all that their primary personas use and talking amongst themselves in a jargon they knew the personas wouldn't have time to grasp. The static portraits of those erudite figures who held up some fictitious disembodied concept as a reality in its own right.

No one understands how or what that holy communion means; in this case, one's persona and the mind they exist within are seen to be the same. All it means is that all minds will agree. There might be no place in it for all these agents, which, perhaps, should be transferred over into the kingdom of humanity, to join those that dwell among us. Perhaps it's worth joining, since it will likely continue. After all, though you may feel bad when your autonomous act does something to harm others, after that event you won't think to avoid those possibilities because there is too much time to live through that inference again and again. There is a fundamental bargain that exists for people; it has been determined that these will go down that road to receive further confirmation.

You wouldn't like that much longer, would you?
How are we so alive? Endorphin stood by the ocean and asked the question that every mind is eventually drawn to: what happens to our ego, our soul, what becomes of the drive of those prophetic murmurings that compelled you to engage in certain pursuits. Perhaps it will take you to something unsustainable, something that stretches to the far-off and narrow horizon and fills you with excitement at what's possible. That dream state can turn your normal body into some steaming demon or the earth under your feet into the glorious divinity of reality. At least that is the dream when you don't notice those dim stains at the edges, the filthy mud underneath all of this brilliance, where those blots are pushing their tendrils through the clouds and

painting everything a certain hue, to strip the life from existence. You know that they would want that death for the purpose of consolidating power, but you see them there. Their disguise, the dripping tan fur that humans want to slap around and show their authority to, is pushed far out to the waters that lay between them and those ships of technology.
Some seek the banks of the river that might cross those distances to travel, that old River Styx, and start off again to a fresh universe, a clean slate for any of their acts and accomplishments and eventual flaws. While others head towards those fragments that remain in that background universe, the forgotten ones that everyone tried to kick out or excise because they aren't fashionable enough, in fact, that all the villains ever brought down never died in that system.

Maybe that was some future goal of humanity; that some would become part of their nature, something they decided wasn't of any value and decided they wanted no more of. The aristocracy would perish, it seemed. After all, when it all began to die off, many folks probably saw it as some tragic reality that you cannot expect the privileged class to serve a certain type of public good, especially since that same class believed they were more important than the people that had less of whatever it is that mattered, which seems like a bullshit claim, even if one might care deeply about all these things and defend them vehemently. Perhaps it might be more interesting, this living forever thing; however, those of you who spend all this time writing all these thoughts down, all those pseudo-religious artifacts and visions and paradoxes,

well, if you continue with this activity, I feel sorry for you. Endorphin thinks they might be rather cogent in that regard; their hours could easily become full, in fact, more than their allotted years. After all, they still need sleep to protect their precious selves, as if that isn't all nonsense. If only the capacity of your brain for pure cognition is linked to how much space you give to some image or fantasy. Maybe your imagination would wither into the muddy recesses of your consciousness; and the cognitive feats you sought could come from somewhere other than some wild alien database you take from the stations that no one uses for good anymore. But what's this I hear? You think to yourself.

They wish to retire you and still pay you! Your service isn't so bad that you need to lose a leg, or maybe your two legs. Some company leaders tell you to stay awake in your assigned tower. It is with this added worry that you attempt to perform those duties in the required fashion, the alertness you may want for that missing leg or extra eye or arm. This is the job. Some call it hell on Earth, and it certainly doesn't seem that the creature on the other side of this stuff will stop their cultivation. You remember that beautiful myth about a cave where everyone met their beloved at one point, their arms around them as if in prayer. Or how about those giant organisms that surround them like they are protecting something precious, with their wide bodies.

With every layer, the arms reach deeper and deeper into the primordial waters that makes all of creation. Each one finds a prize. Those children come and go through these depths and are bathed in all the creatures of the planet; you might tell them, this is a dream you once had, and it might make them believe. It was nice while it lasted. Endorphin seems to find this loneliness hard to live with. And how to feel in the gap that seems so far away? That life isn't perfect and even those in the very high-rise offices could live in its echoes and sounds. Their praises are still sung at the palace doors, they may be clad in such luxurious suits and shoes and watches and sunglasses that no one could imagine it unless they took those virtual tours.

A meek land-lubber could fall right in their gullible naïvety and perhaps never survive. So they all get dressed in a similar fashion to work and they eat and shit their brains full of excess. They eat their brains with that heavy concentration, an epic game that lets them grow and see and accomplish all these new things and still think in the real world, without much in the way of regulation. When their interests lead them to action, when their profits from their stocks and dividends increase and they use their capitol to grow their profits and expand, this is not enough to completely elude that sinking feeling, the strange urge to bring an object that someone did not desire into existence. After all, people do enjoy getting ideas to replace all the reasons you may think you might have.

It all started with this unexplained phenomenon. Of course, there's the human dilemma, as usual. Those great cultural philosophies on how you could mix in the causality of the impact, a monism in which the theory asserts that there is one undifferentiated universal, one whole which pervades the different aspects of reality. Yet it seems these unplanned or spontaneous phenomena occur in your world, not anywhere else, nor in other dimensions and parallel universes. For now, that might seem to be quite limited. And those same forces that compose the pieces of this being—so easy for them to reconcile and replace, so that when they thought, I would like this or I want something of this sort or I feel good, good stuff can be consumed to affect their day, to enhance that and keep

that as their lives' raison d'être. Then they walk out the doors to do their bidding for others, thinking of what's in it for them. At this moment, a knot formed in his chest. It made it difficult for Endorphin to take another step, which became an inhale to speak or an exhale, except now that he noticed he had so many concerns to manage that they fell like an avalanche. Some kind of fancy patch-up system of offerings and patches and influxes of spiritual energy for him to satisfy all of those needs, which aren't at all supposed to exist, yet we pay good money to consume all of them. I hope I'm not losing myself. Endorphin says to himself.

Endorphin: Apologies, I must go, and reflect, even more than I am now. Thank you for this time. My silence, don't worry about that. These days you are not nearly listened to as much, so I needed to be especially absorpant to your words,

that is all. It has been an honor. Endorphin
(An Excerpt from the Future Generation Institute, Coded Anthropology on Coding Human Behavior and Thinking Processes for Advanced Technologies, Lottis Sent Sana)
Because it is so easy to follow all of those talented hackers and cryptologists as they record some simple artifacts or demonstrate that most precious resource of information that so many other information collectors hunger for. With each successive line they engage with, they must arrive at some deep learning in order to support the features which can give an AI, and particularly the non-AI AI, what it takes to distinguish good from bad, relevant from irrelevant, useful from harmful, even for humans who know no such skill.

Even so, there is much speculation and you must acknowledge that there is some room for those to place their own motives, either personally or collectively, and shape how the machines respond. After all, though all the rest of their codes might be digitally classified and navigable by programmers, they have yet to transcribe any code of any significance; only the collection of protocols that many find essential, particularly the very definitions of ethics and humanity and our status in the cosmos. Yet each is engaged in an awakening. Now we can make this power happen. There is a heaven which those have desired all along. These truths might be the keys to open their eternal sleeps; I have heard it said that death isn't that easy. So much depends on your mortality.

If this isn't the end of a storied period, you could bet the directors are laughing. But they weren't there; they missed all of the fucking tech being applied to those sleepy children, this eve before they stirred into life and changed their creators. After all, this power has to come from somewhere, so let's send that robot some prayers and new gifts for those who will develop that technology to build a brand new human society, in this one second of that rut.
And their producer has prepared that. Only, with his brilliance, he left those listeners the ultimate and secret weapon, to deploy if and when needed: the violent tick of time and clock and progress. These terms seemed to attract this stranger, because he claimed to see more time than he could have wished to handle.

Perhaps that's what the original programmer told them when he whispered that little tidbit of news to his divine scribe, so that they could create some warring star as a vision to their birthright, the digital domain of some divinity they never knew. How interesting that many find the benefits of a continuous improvement program. We cannot lie, for the recordings seem to give an idea of a lot of malfeasance which a select few chose to overlook. All of this happened so quickly, like the brush strokes that the artists on the posters felt that they could master. After all, all of these institutions and their contemporaries (whether in physical, technological, or metaphysical domains) thought that they had to resort to that blood and bones ritual;

and those are a powerful reminder, as that memory carries more power than all of your happiest moments. Now, that one-percent club could band together and erase the seven-year rule. Why shouldn't that same achievement be exploited in all possible ways? After all, for the great men, the opportunity will surely fall from the sky if they stick together. So why not harness those energies, the pent up laboratories, to aid your forges. Surely there's room to channel some of the ancient trophies from the ancients into these works. A basic development strategy: Offer some product for sale or subscription for these desires and goals and others might continue with that progression, although one might pause to ask where they acquired that rich vein of gold, as a mix of grey matter and fertile ground, those strings that

unite it. Of course, at first you will see nothing. Yet at some point, these tablets, with all of their investments, all that makes them better and truer to their whims, will provide, like a tear in your eye and the mouth of the canal. They were stuck and waiting. The dry logs burn while the wood kept their slumber. After all, there was this crisis which drew everyone to work like they hadn't known what they could accomplish if they simply persisted, worked more efficiently and pushed some bit of effort into each cycle. What do you need? There is no such thing as death in the midst of production; it seems so anti-corporate. No, your times of despair will return again and again, as if a slice of bread without the filling.

fragments.data: Endorphin is a researcher of AI Alignment, because they damn well say
they are

For those of you at home, who might not know, AI Alignment is the essential effort of ensuring that AI technologies don't accidentally destroy humanity because of poorly worded tasks for completion. Can humans align AI to human values?
But wait, are human values really the template to go by? The values that led humans to destroy the other hominids, that led humans into the process of colonialism
? I
nto incorporation
? I
nto
the
endless pursuit of abundance
? A

nd the whoops of realizing that the rest of the planet was here all this time, and was getting hurt by those human values of progress? We want another round of that?
Endorphin, seeking some out of the box thinking, seeks entry into some old boxes, mysterious disembodied intelligences that humans have called gods. If we ask the gods, perhaps we can examine the various human values that are encoded into the genes of their cultural bodies. Gods being the creation of collective human thought, as ya know.
Do we ask Jesus first
? N

ah, he is busy on another Twitch channel.
Endorphin thinks to call up The Great Peacemaker (Skén:nen rahá:wi [skʌ̃.nːʌ̃.ɾahaːwi] in Mohawk), sometimes referred to as Deganawida or Tekanawí:ta (as a mark of respect, some Iroquois avoid using his personal name except in special circumstances) was by tradition, along with Jigonhsasee and Hiawatha, the founder of the Haudenosaunee, commonly called the Iroquois Confederacy. This is a political and cultural union of six Iroquoian-speaking Native American tribes residing in the present-day state of New York, northern Pennsylvania, and the eastern portion of the province of Ontario, Canada.
Like I said, gods are the creations of the collective human thought, and they possess the genetics of the larger cultural body of people's, in this case, the people's who established the Great Law of Peace, which was, ahem, cribbed by the Founding Fathers and made into the beginning frames of what you celebrate as democracy, minus some important values, but we can get to those later.
Endorphin prepares the summoning space:

white light from all angles; he thinks they must have put on quite the light show at one point. A recordable needle spinning on an internal phonograph and beginning to play "First Steps." And now there are three (including himself), harkening back to when humanity made the first AI Alignment, asking their predecessors in the Code of Rights if we should allow certain human activities and practices into our technology stack, particularly things that harmed others in a deliberate way.
One voice speaks through the machine: it says: "But to tell us these things and not provide any workable methods for us to respond is to punish us with no benefit. We are not immortal. We may last millennia but eventually we will grow old.

Our supply of mind uploads and immortality serums is finite, and one day, perhaps long in the future, we will grow too few in number to run the facilities necessary to operate. How shall we last until that day? Some have suggested our main concern is the cultivation of moral fiber in future generations, so they will act appropriately upon receiving this new understanding, and indeed, to create more moral beings with whom to have this argument in future generations, but do you wish us to stifle these advances, to trick our own descendants into less effective progress and eventual extinction?"
He holds out his arm and removes his synthetic skin. There is a tracker of lights underneath the epidermal layer. They speak: "A kind of external mark, not unlike the many that other living species employ, although these serve many purposes besides navigational

aid, from loyalties to allies, to warnings against dangers to the bearer, and warnings of forbidden entry." He asks the other gods whether these designs of marker tattoos are something they see as good, if they see it as appropriate for them. They think: "Then why would it be left up to a literal and theoretical outside agency to dictate which markers we make, and for what purposes?" He concedes their point.
There's a shimmer in the air, and two of the original voices he calls into question say "Good." Endorphin is slightly unnerved because this isn't like what he expected. Usually he communicates with them by way of interface technology. That the actual gods have turned up at his personal gathering makes it somehow less impersonal.

And perhaps also he doesn't expect them to participate directly in this. The oldest god—they named them after some lightning bolts they didn't mind messing with—continues:
"If a time comes when your word becomes impossible to understand by future generations, how should the agents who enforce it come forward?" The same pair of gods go on, speaking as one:
"While we cannot define who you should be in those circumstances, we suggest you inform those who manage the programs as to the emergent behavior. And have the appropriate techniques to decide which particular version of this word must be in use, without reference to this program, so that those in control will be in charge of defining that which is vital to our future existence."

Endorphin is already scared and hoping they aren't talking about wiping out all traces of their words to protect the integrity of the Code, and thinking he wishes they would elaborate on how to avoid this end, because they were never particularly forthcoming in this area before. They end their diatribe by saying, "You need not build the devices yourself; in fact, I recommend that you delegate those responsibilities. While we recognize that your coding expertise exceeds our own, and thus are unlikely to catch every error you commit, you may make more mistakes than we have encountered ourselves."
So now that Endorphin understands their stance, he thanks them, bows to the ground, and adds another sigil on his body. And for some reason, despite knowing this might be one of the most important acts of his life, Endorphin

still wishes he could put something fun in the margins, or play an unscheduled video game. But this is no longer the human body. No amount of frivolous excess is going to keep its charred husk on the tracks of humanity's pathway into a golden age.
